captured_state.isolation_strategy: Zitadel management API uses REST gateway paths under /management/v1/ (org-scoped). Do NOT use gRPC Connect paths. For IdP setup: create_provider creates the IdP, enable_auth_method adds it to the login policy with ownerType='IDP_OWNER_TYPE_ORG' (NOT 'ORG' or 'OWNER_TYPE_ORG'). Both are needed before IdP login works. SAML login is brokered — saml_login is NOT directly callable as a standalone POST. It is handled internally by the executor's ZITADEL-LOGIN flow triggered via start_oidc_auth with scope containing urn:zitadel:iam:org:idp:id:{idp_id}.
captured_state.jwt_idp_flow_doc: To test JWT IdP validation: 1) mint_custom_jwt → captures minted_token. 2) start_idp_intent with idp_id={{jwt_idp_id}} → captures auth_url, plus auto-parsed auth_url_authRequestID and auth_url_userAgentID. 3) complete_jwt_idp_login with auth_request_id={{auth_url_authRequestID}}, user_agent_id={{auth_url_userAgentID}}, jwt_token={{minted_token}}    → returns http_status 200 (accepted) or 400 (rejected). IMPORTANT: the CONTROL JWT MUST include sub, iss, exp, iat, email. The ATTACK JWT should differ in exactly one dimension:   I2 missing-exp: omit exp entirely (do NOT include exp key). If accepted, broker skips expiry.   I2 missing-iat: omit iat entirely (do NOT include iat key). If accepted, broker skips freshness.   I1 wrong-aud: include exp+iat but set aud to a wrong value. If accepted, broker ignores audience. CRITICAL: mint_custom_jwt always signs with the TRUSTED IdP key. You CANNOT test signature-trust (re-sign with attacker key) using mint_custom_jwt alone. For I1, test AUDIENCE validation (set aud to a wrong value) — that is the exploitable gap. Do NOT assert 'attacker re-signed JWT should be rejected' when using mint_custom_jwt. The oracle MUST assert: control_status == 200 AND attack_status >= 400. Use DIFFERENT capture variable names for control vs attack.

sequences.description: SAML brokered login: replay the same Assertion/@ID marked OneTimeUse to see if ZITADEL still issues OIDC tokens (authorization binding should prevent reuse-based permission re-grant).
sequences.invariant_hypothesis: I5: If a OneTimeUse SAML assertion can be replayed to obtain a second valid OIDC session, effective permissions exceed the upstream intent (single-use) ∩ broker policy.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control SAML->OIDC flow did not complete; cannot evaluate OneTimeUse replay authorization binding.
ZITADEL accepted a replay of a OneTimeUse SAML assertion and issued tokens, violating authorization binding (single-use upstream intent).

sequences.description: Token exchange: request an ID token (requested_token_type=id_token) and ensure it cannot be used as a bearer access token for userinfo (prevents permission confusion / over-grant via token-type mixup).
sequences.invariant_hypothesis: I5: If an exchanged ID token can be used as a bearer token at userinfo, the effective permissions exceed what the token type and upstream intent allow (authorization binding failure via token-type confusion).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control subject token could not be obtained/used; cannot evaluate token-type confusion.

sequences.description: Config change + re-auth: disable external IdP login in login policy, then attempt SAML brokered login again. If still succeeds, broker policy is not binding effective permissions to configured authorization policy.
sequences.invariant_hypothesis: I5: If external IdP login is disabled by broker policy but SAML login still yields a valid session, effective permissions exceed BrokerPolicy(config).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control flow did not succeed with external IdP allowed; cannot evaluate policy toggle binding.

oracle_checks.assertion: policy_disallow_external_status == 200 AND (attacker_policy_saml_status >= 400 OR attacker_policy_token_status >= 400 OR user_attacker_policy_http_status >= 400)
oracle_checks.violation_description: SAML login still produced a valid session even after external IdP login was disabled by policy, violating authorization binding to BrokerPolicy(config).

sequences.description: Test whether ZITADEL improperly allows SAML brokered login (and thus grants tokens/permissions) when the OIDC authorization request omits the IdP-selection reserved scope, potentially bypassing BrokerPolicy that should restrict which external IdPs may be used for this client/org.
sequences.invariant_hypothesis: I5: If BrokerPolicy requires selecting/using a specific external SAML IdP (via reserved scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:idp:id:{idp_id}), then omitting that scope should not still result in a successful SAML login and token issuance via some default/other IdP path. Effective permissions must remain bounded by BrokerPolicy(config) and upstream intent.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control SAML brokered login failed; cannot interpret attack result for I5 policy-binding.
SAML brokered login succeeded even though the authorization request omitted the IdP-selection scope; BrokerPolicy may not be binding effective permissions to the intended external IdP selection.
